context:
Origin: adversarial review of an agent-facing strategy for BenchBox, 2026-11-12. Owner decisions quoted here were made on that date. Line numbers are hints; re-read the cited file before relying on them.

Evidence (2026-11-12): on the DuckDB platform page all seven TPC-H scale factor 10 rows read 'Known defective data' and show scores; on the TPC-H benchmark page the scale factor 1 power table has one ranked row. Benchmark pages already sort excluded rows below ranked ones; platform pages do not.

Related, not duplicated: duckdb-sf10-tpch-defective-datagen-rerun and rerun-cloud-bundles-defective-dbgen replace the defective runs; corpus-tpch-shallow-cohort-replacements-20261018 restores cohort depth. This item changes presentation only.

Decision gate: read the gate ruling first. If the ruling is no-go, do nothing here and ask the owner to drop the item, re-homing the defective-run separation as the gate record proposes. The wording for excluded runs lives in the site repository; reuse it, and stop if changing it would alter ranking policy.

Verification rubric: pass only if the row-count conservation check is run over every summary page and its output is in the PR.

Guardrails: work only in a linked worktree (make worktree-create, then make agent-write-preflight); never edit the primary clone. Related items are delivered together on one feature branch and one PR, as their umbrella item names (site work: BenchBox-dev/benchbox-site); squash-merged. Add a changelog.d fragment for any user-facing change. No live-cloud runs and no credentials in Git or logs. Heavy work (benchmarks, test tiers) runs only through lock-taking entry points or make heavy-run after make heavy-status. Follow the comment policy (make comment-policy-check). Stop and report instead of widening scope; scope removed during review must be re-homed to a named item or dropped by the owner with a reason.

Revision (2026-11-13), after an independent critique and owner decisions: split and deferred.
